facts.statement: The only known species in the genus is Rhomaleopakhus turpanensis.
facts.quote: The type and only species is Rhomaleopakhus turpanensis.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in 1993 by a Chinese-Japanese expedition near Qiketai in Shanshan, Xinjiang province.
facts.quote: The Rhomaleopakhus holotype specimen, IVPP-V11121-1, was found by a Chinese-Japanese Chunichi Shinibun expedition near Qiketai in Shanshan, Xinjiang province in 1993.

facts.statement: The genus name combines Greek words meaning "robust" and "forearm".
facts.quote: The generic name combines the Greek rhomaleos, meaning "robust" and "pakhus, meaning "forearm".

facts.statement: The species name refers to the Turpan Basin where the specimen was collected.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to the Turpan Basin where the specimen was collected.

facts.statement: As a mamenchisaurid sauropod, it was likely a large, four-legged herbivore.
facts.quote: Being a mamenchisaurid sauropod, Rhomaleopakhus was likely a large, quadrupedal herbivore.

facts.statement: Researchers noted that the robust forelimb evolved convergently in core Mamenchisaurus-like taxa, titanosaurs, and ceratopsids.
facts.quote: Upchurch et al. (2021) noted that the robustness of the forelimb, after which the taxon was named, convergently evolved in what are called the "core Mamenchisaurus-like taxa" (CMTs), titanosaurs, and ceratopsids.

facts.statement: Researchers believe the robust forelimb correlates with a flexed forearm orientation, an enhanced role in feeding, and a forward shift in the center of mass.
facts.quote: They believe this correlates with a more flexed orientation of the forearm, an enhanced role of the forearm in feeding, and a more anterior shift in the center of mass.

facts.statement: It is possible that these animals specialized in a feeding strategy involving efficient movement between scattered food sources.
facts.quote: It is possible that CMTs and titanosaurs specialized in a feeding strategy that involved efficient locomotion between sparsely located food sources.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places it as a mamenchisaurid sister taxon to Chuanjiesaurus within a clade that also includes Analong.
facts.quote: They found it to be a mamenchisaurid as the sister taxon to Chuanjiesaurus, in a clade that also includes Analong.

facts.statement: Fossils are known from the lower section of the Kalaza Formation in China's Turpan and Junggar Basins.
facts.quote: Rhomaleopakhus is known from the lower section of the Kalaza Formation in China, one of several fossiliferous formations in the Turpan Basin and Junggar Basin.

facts.statement: The Kalaza Formation dates to the Late Jurassic, lying above Middle Jurassic rocks and below Early Cretaceous layers.
facts.quote: The Kalaza Formation is Late Jurassic in age, overlying the Middle Jurassic-aged Qigu and Shishugou Formations and underlying the Early Cretaceous-aged Tugulu Group.

facts.statement: The formation consists of thick red sandstones and mudstones deposited in terrestrial or river environments.
facts.quote: The Kalaza Formation itself is composed of thick red sandstones in mudstones deposited in terrestrial or fluvial environments.

facts.statement: During the Late Jurassic, the environment was warm and seasonally dry with alluvial deltas, transitioning to arid conditions toward the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It was warm and seasonally dry, though towards the Cretaceous it transitioned to arid or semi-arid, during the Late Jurassic, with alluvial deltas running through the area.

facts.statement: The dinosaur lived in the Late Jurassic Kalaza Formation of China.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en la Formación Kalaza del Jurásico Superior de China.

facts.statement: It lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 145 million years ago in the Tithonian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace 145 millones de años durante el Titoniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The time range for the genus is the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, from 152.21 to 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (152.21 to 143.1 million years ago)
